I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I'm p3 with $795 and just bought ILLINOIS_AVENUE. I'm checking the opponent's holdings to plan my next move.

p1 owns three railroads, St. Charles Place, the Electric Company, and the St. James/Tennessee orange set.

p1 also owns Indiana Avenue and Marvin Gardens. p2 has Mediterranean Avenue, the B&O Railroad, Ventnor Avenue, and Pacific Avenue. p4 owns North Carolina Avenue.

No color set is completable yet. The bank still owns most remaining properties, including Kentucky and Indiana. I'm weighing trade offers to acquire the missing pieces.

Trading Indiana from p1 is unworkable. Neither player can complete the red set without the other and the bank-owned Kentucky. The light blue path remains the priority. I will save cash to buy Oriental and Connecticut.

p1 poses the biggest threat with three railroads and two orange properties. A New York landing would complete their orange set. I am checking whether any trade could block an opponent. I will not mortgage anything since my cash is healthy.

I am now considering trading Illinois Avenue to p1 for one orange property. That would block their orange monopoly and help me complete the light blue set. I need to determine what p1 would want in return.

That trade is unworkable. I would give up a premium red property for an orange worth less than half its value. p1 would gain two reds and only need Kentucky to complete the set. I would block their orange path but still leave them with one orange plus New York unowned. I cannot fully stop them without taking both oranges.

A utility swap is useless. I am now checking p2 and p4 for trade opportunities, but I lack the properties needed to complete their sets.

I will end my turn. I will keep Illinois as a trade chip for the red set and save cash to buy Oriental and Connecticut.
